why: The maximum path sum is the classic tree DP: for each node, the best downward chain is value + max(0, best child chain), and the best path bending at that node is value + both non-negative child chains. Remembering which child each chain uses lets you rebuild the path.
hints: A path has one highest node. What does the path look like on each side of it?
For each node compute down[v] = values[v] + max(0, down[left], down[right]); the best path through v as its top is values[v] + max(0, down[left]) + max(0, down[right]).
Post-order (reverse BFS) computes down[] and the next node on each chain; record the best top node, then print the left chain reversed, the top, and the right chain. O(n).
pitfalls: All values may be negative: the best path is then the single largest node, so never force a child into the path.
Recursion overflows on a 2*10^5 chain; iterate.
Print the path from one end to the other: left chain bottom-up, the top node, then the right chain top-down.
